notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 17 part 2 (Internet Archive buildingengineer1727cont), the 26 weekly issues from 4 July to 26 December 1917. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1916-1919, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1917. In this volume the labels are printed with leader dots and each item is printed once. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name that could not be read on the image, or that fell past a column break and was not found in the next column, was left out. Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or designer named is the owner, shares the owner's surname, is a partner in the owner's firm or is listed at the owner's own address that name is cut too. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit. Completion notices, liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays; issue dates are set from the cover dates (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue, set by hand where the OCR garbled the cover, from the masthead two or four leaves after it), and the item numbers rise issue by issue under those dates. Two single houses that were read against the image and have no name left to publish sit with the held single houses. Three held facts of later volumes whose parcels got a page from this volume were judged and stay held: an Alameda address, and two alterations to a residence where the roll gives flats or a store building.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 17 pt. 2 to 31 read (July 1917 to January 1932); the 5 half-year volumes before July 1917 (1915 to June 1917) are unread, buildingengineer1717cont (January to June 1917) next. In this volume: 85 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but two still need the image check). 325 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 466 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 1,938 numbered entries read, 1,054 San Francisco rows, 588 placed on a parcel, 180 picked and read against the page image, 123 published on 106 pages (47 seeded), 55 held back: 23 alterations with nothing to confirm the street number, 18 storeys, unit counts or uses that contradict the roll, nine pieces of minor work, four repeat listings and one misread street; two more joined the held houses.
